title: Route header banner
description: One announcement in the route header's centre slot: a “Mới” tag, one line of text, an optional date, a pill CTA and a close button. Closed once per user per id (localStorage by default, or your own store). Below md the header's centre is hidden and the same banner is one row at the top of the page content.
when: A short app-wide announcement people should notice for a while: a new feature, a planned maintenance window, a changed price list.
One at a time: the newest announcement replaces the previous one (a new id shows again for everybody).

instead.need: The first visit of a feature, with slides
A message about this page or this record
A search field in the header

a11y: Each copy is role="status"; its close button is named “Đóng thông báo” (locale bannerClose) and has a 44px touch area.
Tab reaches the CTA and then the close button; Enter or Space presses them. Closing moves focus to the next control after the banner (the header's right group, or the page), never to the body.
notes: In AppShell pass header.banner (data, not an element): the shell renders the header copy and the inline copy below md, and closing either hides both. It takes the header's centre in place of header.middle.
A frame of your own: RouteHeader middle={<RouteHeaderBanner {...b} />} plus <RouteHeaderBanner {...b} placement="inline" /> above the page title.
The store is read after mount only, so the server HTML never contains it; with storage blocked it shows, and closing hides it until the next page load.
The text truncates with … first, before the breadcrumb or the right group shrink: one short sentence, the date in sub. The CTA is a Button size="pill" (inverse), never the brand fill.
RouteHeader always renders its three slot containers (left, centre, right): closing the banner never moves the right group.

examples.title: In the route header
examples.description: The header copy and the row copy share one id: close either and both go. The button shows it again (a new id).

examples.title: In AppShell
examples.description: header.banner: the shell renders both copies.
